title: Console sign-out keeps the list layout (column widths, row height, tab order) for the same person; a change of user still clears it
body:
repo:objectstack#1 · os-sales · session_01L6bhgUkbQqRUUFSiu2HGob

Follow-up owed by the maintainer's ruling 7064241116 on #35955 (point 1, option A on the seat's decision card, reviewed by fable first: `build-seat1/35955/pr3/fable-decisions.md` P3-1 in the project folder). Build after #35955 PR3 merges (it defines the browser-only layout keys).

## What happens

#35955 PR3 makes column widths, row height and tab order browser-only (ruling D1). The console's sign-out purge (`ui/packages/auth/src/ActiveOrganizationStorage.ts`, `purgeSignedOutUserClientState`, from #29174 and generalised by #32048) clears every browser key the person wrote, keeping only an exact-match allowlist. #32048 justified that with "server preferences are untouched, re-login gets them back"; after PR3 there is no server copy, so every sign-out or ended session resets everyone's list layout. Filters, sorts and search terms are in-memory drafts since #36026, so what remains under these keys is object names, field names, widths and view ids, no record data.

## To do

1. The sign-out tier of the purge keeps the list layout keys PR3 introduces (a prefix exception, the first one), and the grid's own width copies (`grid-columns-…`, `ui/packages/plugin-grid/src/objectGridColumnState.ts`) so a related tab's widths (browser-only by ruling 7064246280 on #35892) behave the same. The change-of-user tier (`purgePreviousUserClientState`) does NOT keep them.
2. A test pins what may live under the kept keys (widths, row height, tab order only), so nothing else can hide from the purge later. No `anon` key spelling.
3. Update the P1 checklist item `identity-auth.console-sign-out-and-ended-session` and `ui/packages/auth/README.md` (the sign-out section). `@object-ui/auth` is published: changeset.

## Acceptance

- Adjust a list's column widths and row height, sign out, sign back in as the same person on the same browser: they are still there.
- Sign out, sign in as a different person on that browser: the list opens at the view's defaults; none of the first person's keys remain.
- A session that ends on its own behaves like a sign-out.
